title: LeaveWorkspaceFlow
wrapsNative: alert(_:isPresented:actions:message:) for the blocked case; sheet(isPresented:content:) with presentationDetents and interactiveDismissDisabled for the confirmation, holding MonarchConsequenceList, MonarchInlineNotice and MonarchButtons
summary: A recipe, not a component: a member leaves a workspace after a confirmation that lists what they lose and what stays, or learns why they cannot leave yet and how to fix it.
whenToUse: In workspace settings, for a member who wants to leave a shared workspace.
whenNotToUse: To remove someone else, use the revoke access recipe. To delete the workspace for everyone, ask with MonarchStepUpAuthDialog and a type-to-confirm field.
api: .alert("You can’t leave yet", isPresented: $isBlocked) { Button("Transfer ownership") { … }; Button("Close", role: .cancel) {} } message: { Text(reason) }
.sheet(isPresented: $isConfirming) { MonarchConsequenceList([…]); MonarchButton("Leave workspace", variant: .danger, isLoading: isLeaving, fullWidth: true) { … } }

states.name: confirm
states.description: A sheet with the title naming the workspace, a line saying it happens at once, the consequence list and a danger Leave workspace button with Cancel.

states.name: leaving
states.description: Leave workspace shows its spinner; Cancel is disabled and the sheet cannot be swiped away.

states.name: failed
states.description: A danger MonarchInlineNotice in the sheet; the person can try again.

states.name: blocked
states.description: When the person is the last owner, or the app has another reason, the button opens an alert that says why and offers the fix (Transfer ownership) instead of leaving.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component or a system alert in the theme: the heading style title, MonarchConsequenceList with its kind icons, the danger and ghost MonarchButtons.
platformNotes: The web's LeaveWorkspaceFlow is one component built on ConfirmDialog and Dialog. On iOS it is a recipe: a system alert cannot hold a list or stay open while a request runs, so the confirmation is a sheet (which keeps the pending and error states inside it), and the blocked case, which only needs a sentence and two buttons, is a system alert. The web's default consequences and messages are written in the app here. The web's fixAction can be any element; in the alert it is a button. The parity map lists alert (MonarchBanner on iOS) as a part; the blocked explanation is a short modal message with a fix, which on iOS is the system alert, so MonarchBanner is not used. Android composes the same recipe.
accessibility: The sheet's title has the header trait.
MonarchConsequenceList reads each consequence with its kind, so removed, kept and warning do not depend on the icon.
The alert is the system's, read in full by VoiceOver with its buttons; Close has the cancel role.
Buttons are MonarchButtons with 44-point touch targets and a busy state while leaving.
The sheet cannot be dismissed while leaving, so the result is not lost.
edgeCases: Check whether the person is the last owner on the server as well; the recipe's check only decides which dialog opens.
After leaving, navigate away from the workspace: its screens are no longer available.
List the apps the person loses by name when the workspace has several.
